title: PPFD, DLI, Watts and Joules: Understanding Light Measurements in Agriculture
intro: Light is one of the most important factors affecting plant growth, but light sensors can report their measurements in several different ways.

They all measure light in some way, but they do
not
tell you the same thing. The easiest way to understand the difference is:

items.text: PPFD tells you how much useful plant light is available right now.
DLI tells you how much useful plant light the crop received throughout the day.
W/m² tells you how much light energy is arriving right now.
J/m² tells you how much light energy accumulated over a period of time.

PPFD and DLI are particularly useful for plants. Watts and joules are measurements of physical energy.
PPFD
stands for
Photosynthetic Photon Flux Density
. The name sounds complicated, but the idea is simple:
PPFD tells us how much light that plants can use for photosynthesis is reaching them right now.
PPFD is normally displayed as
µmol/m²/s
. For most growers, understanding the exact scientific meaning of this unit is not particularly important. The important part is:
A higher PPFD means more photosynthesis-capable light is reaching the plant at that moment.
Think of PPFD as being similar to a
speedometer
. A speedometer tells you how fast your car is travelling
right now
. PPFD tells you how much useful growing light is reaching the crop
right now
An example.
Imagine checking a greenhouse throughout the day. You might see:
The sunlight changes throughout the day, so PPFD changes with it. PPFD is therefore very useful when you want to know things such as:

items.text: How much light is reaching the crop right now?
Is part of the greenhouse being shaded?
How much light is reaching plants underneath a shade curtain?
How much additional light are grow lights providing?
How does light differ between different areas of a greenhouse?

content.text: DLI
stands for
Daily Light Integral
. DLI answers a slightly different and often more useful question:
How much usable light did the plant receive during the entire day?
DLI is normally displayed as
mol/m²/day
. You can simply think of this as:
The total amount of growing light received today.
If PPFD is like your car's
speedometer
, DLI is similar to the
distance travelled during the day
. PPFD might constantly change, but DLI keeps adding the light together as the day progresses.
Consider two different days.

items.text: the morning is extremely sunny, but heavy clouds arrive during the afternoon.
the sunlight is not quite as strong, but the sky remains clear throughout the entire day.

content.text: Looking at only the highest PPFD measurement could make Day 1 appear better. But the plants might actually receive
more total light on Day 2
DLI makes this easy to see because it adds together the usable light received throughout the whole day. For example:
Monday reached a much higher light level. But Tuesday provided considerably more usable light over the entire day. For crop production, that can be much more meaningful.
PPFD and DLI should not really be thought of as competing measurements. They answer two different questions.

how much useful light has the crop received today?

Another common way of measuring light is
watts per square meter
, written as
W/m²
. You may also encounter
mW/m²
. A milliwatt is simply one-thousandth of a watt.
These measurements tell us:
How much light energy is reaching an area right now.
This is useful in many applications. For example, solar radiation sensors frequently measure sunlight in W/m². Strong sunlight reaching the Earth's surface may be around

sections.heading: Why aren't watts always ideal for plants?

content.text: Plants do not respond to every type of light in exactly the same way. A measurement in watts tells us
how much energy is present
, but it does not necessarily tell us
how many useful photons are available for photosynthesis
Imagine two different lights that both produce
500 W/m²

. One could produce light that is very useful for photosynthesis, while another could contain considerably more energy outside the wavelengths we are interested in for plant growth. The energy measurement may be the same, while their usefulness to a plant may be different.
That is why agricultural lighting commonly uses
PPFD instead of simply measuring watts
A
joule
is a measurement of energy. When light energy is added together over time, it can be expressed using joules. For example,
J/m²
means the amount of energy that has reached one square meter.
The relationship between watts and joules is similar to the relationship between PPFD and DLI.

content.text: The major difference is
what is being counted
. PPFD and DLI are concerned with the photons used for photosynthesis. Watts and joules are concerned with energy.

sections.heading: Why do plants use PPFD instead of watts?

content.text: Plants perform photosynthesis using individual packets of light called
photons
. PPFD essentially counts the amount of photosynthetically useful light reaching the plant.

This is important because different colors of light contain different amounts of energy. For example, a blue photon contains a different amount of energy from a red photon. A measurement based purely on watts measures that energy difference. For photosynthesis, however, we are often more interested in
how many usable photons are reaching the plant
This is why PPFD has become such an important measurement in horticulture and controlled-environment agriculture.

sections.heading: Can W/m² be converted to PPFD?

content.text: Sometimes, but there is an important limitation. To accurately convert light energy into PPFD, you need to know something about the
colors or wavelengths contained in the light
. This is because different wavelengths contain different amounts of energy.

With natural sunlight, approximate conversions can sometimes be made because the spectrum of sunlight is reasonably predictable. With artificial lighting, the situation can be very different. For example, these can all have different light spectra:
Two lights could therefore produce the same W/m² measurement while producing different PPFD measurements. For accurate agricultural measurements, it is generally better to
measure PPFD directly with an appropriate sensor

sections.heading: Which measurement is best for agriculture?

content.text: If the purpose is understanding the light available for
crop growth and photosynthesis
, PPFD and DLI are generally the most useful measurements.
Use PPFD when you want to know:

items.text: Light levels at different canopy heights
Changes caused by curtains, films or greenhouse coverings

content.text: Use DLI when you want to know:

items.text: How much light the crop received today
Whether crops are receiving enough light over time
Differences between sunny and cloudy days
Whether supplemental lighting may be required
How effectively supplemental lighting is increasing daily light exposure

content.text: For most growers,
DLI can be one of the easiest measurements to use when looking at overall crop-light conditions
. Instead of asking "How bright did it get at noon?", DLI lets us ask:
"Did the crop receive enough light today?"
That is often the more useful agricultural question.

sections.heading: When are W/m² and joules useful?

content.text: PPFD and DLI are not always the correct measurement. W/m² and J/m² are useful when the goal is measuring
energy rather than photosynthesis
. Examples include:
If the question is
"How much solar energy is arriving?"
, W/m² may be appropriate. If the question is
"How much useful growing light is reaching my crop?"
, PPFD is normally more useful.

sections.heading: Which measurement should a grower look at?

content.text: A simple way to choose is:

items.text: How much useful plant light is available right now?
How much useful plant light did the crop receive today?
How much solar energy is arriving right now?
How much solar energy accumulated over time?

If you remember only four things, remember these:

items.text: PPFD = useful plant light right now
DLI = total useful plant light today

content.text: For most agricultural applications concerned with plant growth,
PPFD and DLI provide the most directly useful information
. PPFD shows what is happening now. DLI shows the bigger picture. Together, they make it much easier to understand how much light a crop is actually receiving.
